summary: Rest day at Capitol Reef NP (goat farm lunch, Curry Pizza dinner), then a 70-mile day with about 6,000 ft of climbing and 6,000 ft of descent into Escalante UT, ending at a lakeside campground.
slept_at: Lakeside campground near Escalante UT (name not stated)
planning_notes: Capitol Reef to Escalante UT is a hard 70-mile day: about 6,000 ft up and 6,000 ft down, with a long gravel mountainside descent into Escalante.
A local goat farm near Capitol Reef served a good lunch (bread, pesto, cheese); worth asking about on a rest day.

summary: Rode 84 miles from Milford UT to Baker NV, crossing into Pacific Time, then took a rest day in Baker NV (population 36) at the Stargazer Inn hostel and its general store.
contacts: Liz and James, owners of the Stargazer Inn hostel and general store, Baker NV
planning_notes: Baker NV has about 36 residents, so options are very limited; the hostel's general store was the team's base for the rest day and where they ate ice cream.

summary: Support-car day: the blogger drove while the bikers rode 63 miles from Baker to Ely NV; the team stopped at the Great Basin visitor center and stayed at a La Quinta in Ely, where a planned learning festival had been cancelled due to COVID and they packed goodie bags for kids.
learning_festival: Ely NV learning festival was planned but cancelled due to COVID; team packed goodie bags for the expected kids
planning_notes: La Quinta in Ely is right next to a grocery store, convenient for resupply at the end of a ride.
Bristlecone general store in Baker has a wall of books and is a good place to wait for the bikers during a long support-car gap.

summary: Rode US-50 ('the Loneliest Road') from Ely to Eureka NV (78 miles); a thunderstorm soaked the team with cold rain and no cell service meant they could not reach the driver, so they shuttled the last stretch and got ice cream and a Highway 50 stamp in Eureka.
slept_at: Hotel in Eureka NV (name not stated)
contacts: La Quinta, Ely NV (comped the team's rooms)
planning_notes: US-50 in Nevada: the car met the team for water/snack stops about 28 miles apart, so carry food and water for that stretch.
No cell service on US-50 in Nevada: the team could not reach the driving support car during a storm, so agree on meeting points and check-in times.
Nevada thunderstorms near Eureka came on fast with cold rain. The team had left their rain jacket in the car; carry one even on hot days.

Stamp books from the Baker general store: collect a stamp in each US-50 town and mail them to Travel Nevada for an 'I survived the loneliest road' certificate. Eureka's general store and malt shop are on the route.

summary: Biked 63 miles on US-50 from Eureka to Austin NV and saw wild mustangs; a twisted ankle put one rider in the car after 10 miles, and the planned housing fell through when the town park banned overnight camping, so the team stayed at an RV campsite.
slept_at: RV campsite in Austin NV (after the town park said no overnight camping)
contacts: Baker Foundation at MIT (funded the pre-trip bike repair and safety workshop)
planning_notes: Austin NV: the town park has a 'no overnight camping' sign and sprinklers. Confirm a real campsite by phone before arriving; the team had only a verbal OK from town and ended up at an RV campsite.

Pre-trip bike repair and safety workshop (tubes, brakes, chains, city safety) was funded by the Baker Foundation at MIT; the tools bought for it became the team's roadside repair toolbox. Chains needed frequent cleaning on the trip.
Planned 3 AM wake / 5 AM start for early-morning riding never happened (team slept until 9 AM). If you want early starts, set the alarm and expectations the night before.
A minor ankle twist from a fall on stairs was enough to put a rider in the car for the rest of the day; have a car-swap plan for injuries.

summary: Longest day of the trip: 112 miles from Austin to Fallon NV (2,615 ft of elevation drop per the post) across salt flats and desert, with lunch at Middlegate Station, wild horses running alongside, and arrival at the Fallon Youth Center for a learning festival.
learning_festival: Taught a learning festival from the Fallon Youth Center over the next few days
contacts: Fallon Youth Center, Fallon NV (hosted the team for several days)
planning_notes: Austin to Fallon NV is 112 miles. Middlegate Station, halfway, is the only stop (burger joint, motel, gas station); the team did not stay there, so carry water and food for the rest of the day.
US-50 near Fallon has a fair amount of car traffic, so the road is not as lonely as its nickname suggests; plan for passing cars near the Fallon end.
Evening water break with the car is worth planning for on long days; the team met the car roughly every 20 to 28 miles.

summary: Rest day in Fallon NV: slept at the Fallon Youth Club, a visit from host Shannon and her dog, a rib cook-off, groceries at Lattin Farms and Walmart (last box of Clif Bars), and dinner of fire tacos by Shannon.
slept_at: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon NV (couch in the Recreation Center)
learning_festival: Preparing for the final learning festival at the Fallon Youth Club (solar cell workshop)
contacts: Shannon, Fallon Youth Club, Fallon NV (coordinated the learning festival and cooked the team's meals)
planning_notes: Fallon NV is a real resupply stop: Walmart and Lattin Farms (known for cantaloupe) are both there.
Waiting in a sunny parking lot in flip-flops gave one rider a sunburned foot; sunscreen the feet or wear closed shoes on rest days in town.
Sleeping on the hard, boomerang-shaped couch at the Fallon Youth Club caused a rider back pain the next day. Bring your own sleeping pad.

summary: Last learning festival of the trip, at the Fallon Youth Club on a Sunday with low turnout (schools started the next day); the team reflected that their workshops moved from content-heavy to hands-on and engagement-driven.
learning_festival: Final learning festival at the Fallon Youth Club; students played pool, basketball and ping pong during breaks; a workshop was missing because a team member was away
contacts: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon NV (learning festival host)
planning_notes: Circuits workshop lesson: 1.5-hour sessions were too short for younger students to retain advanced concepts like parallel circuits and Ohm's law. Skip most slides and go straight to hands-on building (add LEDs or buzzers, let kids pick LED colors).
Timing: schools in Fallon NV started the day after this LF, so late-August events drew low turnout. Book learning festivals around the school calendar, and check when local schools start.
Engagement beat content in every workshop (soap-bubble structural color demo; CAD demo where kids chose the design). Plan activities kids can make and keep.
With one team member away, the team could only run part of their workshop lineup; plan for a missing team member by keeping workshops that one person can run alone.

summary: Fallon to Carson City NV (63 miles, 1,500 ft of gain); the team picked up Robert after his COVID isolation in Reno, rejoined the bikers, and had a rib dinner with host Tod on a hilltop. The post also launched a Q&A for blog readers.
slept_at: Tod's home, Carson City NV (on a hilltop)
contacts: Tod, Carson City NV (host; rib dinner)
Reno Suites, Reno NV (where Robert isolated with COVID)
planning_notes: COVID: a team member tested positive. The team dropped him at Reno Suites for isolation, then the car rejoined him later. Plan a sick-member isolation place and a way to get the rider back to the team.
Host homes were often on hilltops, so expect a climb on arrival.

summary: Carson City NV to Lake Tahoe CA (47 miles, 3,900 ft of gain) with host Tod riding along; camped at Emerald Bay, which had water on both sides; the team also listed the many items lost over the trip.
slept_at: Emerald Bay campground, Lake Tahoe CA
contacts: Tod, Carson City NV (rode with the team to Lake Tahoe and back)
planning_notes: Emerald Bay campground at Lake Tahoe CA has water on both sides of the site and is worth planning for.
US-50 goes from the empty Nevada 'loneliest road' to a busy highway in California near Tahoe; expect much more traffic.
Lost items over the trip: chargers, socks, glasses, sunglasses, sleeping bag, shoes, and two water bottles that fell off bikes unnoticed. Check bottle cages and keep chargers in one bag.
Left a rider's shoes at the host's home in Carson City; the team drove an hour back to retrieve them. Check the host area before leaving.

summary: Rode 103 miles from South Lake Tahoe to Sacramento CA, the team's first six-biker day, with friend Kellie riding 60 miles over the Sierras; a route mistake onto a Highway 50 freeway led to a back-road detour, and the day ended with a church dinner at a host's home in Sacramento.
slept_at: Hyatt Place, Sacramento CA (per the next day's post; not stated in this one)
contacts: Kellie (rode the first 60 miles on a clipped-in bike)
Sam, Sacramento CA (opened his home for the church dinner)
planning_notes: Highway 50 near Sacramento becomes a large freeway with unwelcoming signs and traffic; the team got off it and took back roads into suburbs.
The Jedediah Smith bike trail (last ~13 miles into Sacramento) is a car-free path, good for the end of a long day.
Running traffic lights as a group split the riders; one rider got stuck on a red. Pick a regroup point at each light.

summary: Sacramento to Vacaville CA (56 miles, 243 ft of gain) on a river path and bike trails, with an In-N-Out lunch in Davis; the post is a reflection on music played along the trip and on lessons about group living and cycling.
slept_at: Hotel in Vacaville, CA (name not stated)
contacts: Amira (met the team for lunch, Davis CA)
Music school director, Hazard KY (offered a campus tour; team's workshop was in Hazard)
Johnson Wabash School, Ferguson MO (lent the team a piano; teachers shared stories)
Denine, music teacher next door to a host in Utah
planning_notes: Between Sacramento and Vacaville, free water and ice at gas stations was hard to find, unlike small Midwest towns. Buy a small item when you fill up.

Sacramento to Davis has good bike infrastructure: a river path and a bike path beside a freeway kept the team off car roads for most of the morning. The team hit 21 mph at their fastest on the river path.
In-N-Out in Davis CA: the post half-jokingly suggests In-N-Out as a future sponsor.
Ask schools for loaner instruments for learning-festival demos: Johnson Wabash School in Ferguson MO had two pianos and lent one to the team.

summary: Final ride, Vacaville to San Francisco (73.2 miles, 1,909 ft of gain), finishing over the Golden Gate Bridge at sunset with friends and family waiting; the post also tallies trip totals and names foam sleeping pads as the team's MVP.
contacts: Maxwell's parents (hosted a home-cooked meal after the finish)
planning_notes: Foam sleeping pads were the team's MVP: a seat at lunch, a sleep pad, rain shelter, blanket, pillow, and car sunshade. Pack foam pads.

Trip totals for five riders over about 80 days: Clif bars ~500, electrolyte tablets/packets ~500, peanut butter jars 10+ (some Costco-size), chamois butter packets ~10 (mostly unused), ice cream stops 10+, 8 state lines. Useful for food budgeting.
A tiny hand pump got stuck and released all its air while the team helped cyclists in Sausalito. Carry a reliable pump.
Bay Area suburbs had few public restrooms: the team tried three gas stations and a coffee shop, and ended at a Whole Foods. Plan restroom and water stops for the last stretch.
The Golden Gate Bridge had gusts near 20 mph; bring a wind layer for the crossing.
